sections.h1: Channel Letter Signs in New York City for Storefronts and Buildings
sections.lead_html:
Channel letters are individually built, three-dimensional letters lit from inside by LEDs and mounted directly to your building.

Vision Graphics designs and makes custom channel letter signs for NYC storefronts and buildings, in front-lit, halo-lit, and combination styles, and manages installation through licensed partners.

sections.intro_html: Each letter is its own shallow metal can with a face, a return, LEDs, and a back. Outdoor sign letters built this way are made for night visibility.

items.title: Faces
items.html: The face is the lit or solid front of the letter. Front-lit letters use translucent acrylic, and halo-lit letters use a solid face.

items.title: Returns
items.html: The returns are the sides, usually aluminum. They add depth and side color to each letter.

items.title: LEDs
items.html: LED modules sit inside each letter. LED channel letters run on a power supply, and even module spacing keeps the face evenly lit.

items.title: Backs
items.html: The back closes the letter and carries the mounting. Front-lit letters have an opaque back, and halo-lit letters have a clear back that lets the light wash the wall. Trimless channel letters leave off the trim cap for a cleaner edge.

sections.html:
Front-lit, halo-lit, combination, and open-face letters look different, cost different amounts, and meet landmark rules differently. Halo-lit letters are also called reverse channel letters, and halo-lit signage pairs a solid face with a glow behind it. Backlit or illuminated channel letters come in all four styles.

sections.intro_html: How the letters attach to your facade changes the look, wiring, and permit drawings.

items.title: Raceway
items.html: A metal box behind the letters that houses the wiring and power supply. Raceway signage simplifies the electrical hookup, and channel letters on raceway mounts suit uneven walls or buildings with limited drilling.

items.title: Flush (Direct) Mount
items.html: Letters attach directly to the wall, with wiring routed behind. Flush mounting gives the cleanest look on solid masonry, and it needs precise wall penetrations.

items.title: Backer Panel
items.html: Letters mount to a flat panel that mounts to the wall. A backer panel evens out a rough surface and can make removal easier at the end of a lease.

sections.html:
Size letters for the viewer. A common rule of thumb is about one inch of letter height for every 10 feet of viewing distance, and we confirm the size on a drawing of your facade.

Send your logo files and brand color codes. We match the face and return colors on the drawing you approve, and we choose an LED color temperature that fits your brand. On landmarked buildings, letter height may be capped at 18 inches.

sections.h2: How Much Do Channel Letter Signs Cost in NYC?
sections.html:
Most channel letter signs for an NYC storefront cost roughly $4,000 to $12,000, depending on letter height, lighting type, and mounting. Small sets start near $3,000, and large or complex sets cost more.

TypePlanning rangeWhat drives it
Front-lit$3,000 to $12,000Letter count and height, LED specification, raceway or flush mount
Halo-lit$5,000 to $15,000Solid faces, clear backs and standoffs, about 15% to 30% above front-lit
CombinationFrom about $5,000A lit face and a halo, about 25% to 40% above front-lit

Treat these planning ranges as a guide to channel letter sign prices. They are not quotes. Permits, electrical work, and installation are separate lines, and we itemize each quote. Request a quote for your address.

sections.intro_html: Lit channel letters are regulated in New York City. Your sign may need several approvals, and the list depends on its size, lighting, mounting, and location.

items.title: Sign Permit
items.html: A lit sign may require a DOB sign permit. Lit channel letters are illuminated signs, so plan for one.

items.title: Electrical and Illuminated Sign Permits
items.html: A lit sign may require a separate electrical permit filed by a licensed electrician. A lit sign that extends beyond the building line may also require an annual illuminated sign permit.

items.title: Zoning
items.html: Your zoning district sets how large a sign can be and how it may be lit. We check the rules for your address before the design is final.

items.title: Landmarks and Historic Districts
items.html:
LPC staff cannot approve internally illuminated exterior signs, including front-lit letters. They may approve halo-lit letters with solid faces and a concealed light source, pin-mounted up to 18 inches tall and projecting no more than two inches.

Standard channel letter depths may exceed that limit, and other designs may need a public hearing, so ask our team before you design.

items.title: Landlord and Building Approval
items.html: Your landlord may require approval of the drawings, and some leases set their own sign rules. Send your lease's sign guidelines early.

items.title: Licensed Installation
items.html: A licensed sign hanger may be required to install or supervise the work, with exemptions for small signs. Our licensed installation partners handle the filing and installation, and our team prepares the drawings.

items.title: Existing Signs and Local Law 15 of 2026
items.html: NYC has temporary protections through February 8, 2028 for certain accessory signs that were in place by February 9, 2025. They do not make a noncompliant sign lawful, and they do not cover a new replacement sign. Ask our team about your letters.

steps: Drawing approval: You approve a drawing showing letter size, lighting type, color, and mounting.

sections.h2: Channel Letters for Restaurants and Retail
sections.intro_html: Channel letters in NY suit shops, restaurants, and offices. For channel letter signs, Manhattan businesses order; see signs for Manhattan. Choosing between lit and unlit letters? See our dimensional letter signs and storefront signs.

items.title: Restaurants
items.html: Letters that pull diners in after dark. NYC restaurant owners choose channel letter signs they can read from across the street, and halo-lit styles add a warm glow. Learn more about signs for restaurants.

items.title: Retail
items.html: Consistent branding from the street to the sales floor. Front-lit letters carry a bright brand color across one store or many. Learn more about signs for retail.

items.title: Building Signs
items.html: Letters that name a building or a tenant. Building signs use larger channel letters on a facade or parapet.

items.q: How much do channel letter signs cost?
items.a_html: Most channel letter signs for an NYC storefront cost roughly $4,000 to $12,000, and small sets start near $3,000. Halo-lit letters typically cost about 15% to 30% more than front-lit, and combination letters about 25% to 40% more. Letter height drives the price the most, and we itemize each quote.

Usually yes. A lit sign may require a DOB sign permit and a separate electrical permit, and a lit sign that extends beyond the building line may also need an annual illuminated sign permit. Zoning applies, and landmark districts add review. We prepare the drawings and coordinate the licensed filer.

Front-lit letters give the highest night visibility and are simpler to service. Halo-lit letters give a refined glow on the wall behind them, and they may be easier to approve on a landmarked building. Combination letters give both. Send a photo of your facade, and we will recommend one.

items.q: How long do the LEDs last?
items.a_html: Quality LED modules are rated around 50,000 hours to 70% of their original brightness, which is about 12 years at 12 hours a day. The power supply can wear out sooner, so periodic checks keep the sign lit evenly. Ask our team about maintenance and coverage for your letters.

Most projects run about six to ten weeks from approved drawing to installation, including permits. Fabrication and shipping take about three to five weeks, and permit and landmark review vary by sign and address. Tell us your target date, and we will confirm the schedule in your quote.

items.q: Can you repair or replace existing letters?
items.a_html: Yes, our team can assess them and advise if a repair or a replacement makes sense. A replacement sign is new work that may need its own permit, and Local Law 15 of 2026 protections do not cover a new sign. Send us photos of your letters to start.

items.q: Can channel letters go on a landmarked building?
items.a_html: Sometimes. LPC staff cannot approve internally illuminated exterior signs, which includes front-lit letters. They may approve halo-lit letters with solid faces and a concealed light source, pin-mounted up to 18 inches tall and projecting no more than two inches. Other designs may need a public hearing, so ask our team first.
